source.quote: Every request MUST include the required `meta` fields; see `meta`.
The cursor is an opaque string token, representing a position in the result set; Page size is determined by the server, and clients MUST NOT assume a fixed page size

requirements.exclusion: Forbids an assumption. A client that assumed a fixed page size and one that did not send identical requests — the assumption only shows in how the client interprets what comes back, which is not on the wire.

source.quote: Servers SHOULD: Provide stable cursors; Handle invalid cursors gracefully

requirements.exclusion: Cursor stability is a property across time and sessions — the same cursor presented later must still resolve — which one recording cannot exhibit. The graceful half is stated concretely by PAGE-011, which is excluded at this revision for the reason it records.

source.quote: Clients SHOULD: Treat a missing `nextCursor` as the end of results; Support both paginated and non-paginated flows

requirements.exclusion: Both bind how a client reads a result it already has. Stopping because `nextCursor` was absent and stopping for any other reason produce the same session: no further request.

source.quote: Clients MUST treat cursors as opaque tokens: Don't make assumptions about cursor format; Don't attempt to parse or modify cursors; Don't make any determination based on cursor value other than whether a non-null value was provided (e.g. an empty string is a valid cursor and thus MUST NOT be treated as the end of results)

requirements.exclusion: A recording's witness for a cursor the client made up — one no result in the session issued — does not hold at this revision. 2026-07-28 drops 2025-11-25's "Don't persist cursors across sessions" and has no sessions to persist across; its caching page says "When a cached page expires, the client SHOULD re-fetch that page using its cursor", a cursor issued before the recording began. A parsed or altered cursor is indistinguishable on the wire from such a one.

source.quote: Invalid cursors SHOULD result in an error with code -32602 (Invalid params).

requirements.exclusion: Whether a cursor is invalid is the server's knowledge. At 2025-11-25 a cursor no result in the session issued witnesses it (cursors must not outlive a session, and 2025-11-25's PAGE-003 judges that); at this revision a cursor issued before the recording began is a valid one the client should re-present (server/utilities/caching), so a server accepting it may be conforming. The everything server still rejects cursors its own scheme did not issue; the probe capture exercises that.
